result.final_text:
## What this letter says

You went to the hospital emergency department. You fell at home and hit your head. You did not pass out (no loss of consciousness).

You had an X-ray of your right hip. There is no broken bone (fracture).

You had a detailed X-ray scan of your head (CT scan). It showed no bleeding inside the head.

Your blood pressure was 142/80 lying down. It was 108/66 standing up. This means your blood pressure drops when you stand up (postural hypotension).

## What you need to do

1. Stop taking amlodipine 10 milligrams.
2. Keep taking all your other medicines.
3. Stand up slowly. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand.
4. You have been sent to the Falls Prevention Clinic. The clinic will write to you with an appointment.
5. Your family doctor (GP) will check your blood pressure again in 4 weeks. They will check it lying down and standing up.

## Dates and medicines

- 14 October 2026: you were seen in hospital.
- In 4 weeks: your family doctor (GP) will check your blood pressure lying down and standing up.
- Amlodipine 10 milligrams: stop. It may be making your blood pressure drop when you stand.
- All other medicines: keep taking them.

## Questions to ask your doctor

- When will my family doctor check my blood pressure?
- How long will it take the Falls Prevention Clinic to write to me?
- Which of my medicines should I keep taking?

## When to get urgent help

In the next few days, call 999 or go to A&E (the hospital emergency department) if you get:

- a headache that gets worse
- vomiting (being sick)
- confusion
- drowsiness (feeling very sleepy)

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
